newsitem.title: CHINA: China to up stamp tax on stock trading to 0.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: China to up stamp tax on stock trading to 0.5 pct.

text.p: China's State Council, or cabinet, has decided to raise the stamp tax on stock trading to 0.5 percent from May 10, the Xinhua news agency said on Friday.
The stamp tax on stock trading is currently 0.3 percent.
China's stock markets fell heavily on Thursday on talk that the securities authorities would introduce measures, including raising stamp tax, to cool down the market.
"This in itself won't bring the markets down," said Bruce Richardson, chief representative for Hoare Govett Asia Ltd in Shanghai.
"It does, however, send a signal that the government wants to bring the market down," he said.
The announcement came after the market closed on Friday.
Brokers said the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock markets may fall slightly on Monday but the fall would be limited.
"It will fall one or two percent only," said an analyst at a foreign brokerage in Shanghai. "This is too small a change to have any impact."
